The proof uses inverse-probability cancellation.  Fix \(z\in\{0,1\}\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a bounded measurable \(g\).  Positivity of the covariate cell and treatment overlap make conditioning on \((Z=z,X=x)\) well defined.  Consistency and conditional exchangeability give
\[
 \mathcal L(D,R\mid Z=z,X=x)=\mathcal L(D(z),R(z)\mid X=x)=\mu_{zx}.
\]
Since \(L=\min\{D,\tau\}\) is measurable with respect to \((D,R)\), arm-specific independent censoring gives
\[
 E_P(\Delta\mid D,R,Z=z,X=x)
 =\Pr(C\ge L\mid D,R,Z=z,X=x)=G_{zx}(L).
\]
The full-horizon support assumption gives \(G_{zx}(L)\ge\gamma>0\), so division is legitimate.  Applying iterated expectation, first for nonnegative \(g\) and then to the positive and negative parts, yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[\left.\frac{\Delta g(D,R)}{G_{zx}(L)}\right|Z=z,X=x\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[\left.
   \frac{g(D,R)}{G_{zx}(L)}E_P(\Delta\mid D,R,Z=z,X=x)
   \right|Z=z,X=x\right]\\
 &=E_P\{g(D,R)\mid Z=z,X=x\}\\
 &=\int_{\mathcal E^2}g\,d\mu_{zx}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
On \(\Delta=1\), the observed history determines the truncated pair: if death occurs by \(\tau\), the history ends at that death and records whether and when readmission occurred; if death does not occur by \(\tau\), completion through \(\tau\) records the horizon-survivor atom and the readmission history.  The administrative at-risk path in \(O\) determines \(G_{zx}\), and its lower bound makes the displayed inverse weight unique on the whole relevant support.  Indicator choices for \(g\), followed by a monotone-class argument, therefore recover every Borel cell of \(\mu_{zx}\), including \(D(z)=\infty\).  Thus \(\mu_{zx}\) is a functional of \(P=\mathcal L(O)\), rather than an additional observed-law definition.

The proof uses conditional stochastic-order coupling and an explicit measurable quantile lift.  For a fixed \(x\), call a probability law \(Q_x\) on \(\mathcal E^4\) compatible when its \((D(0),R(0))\) margin is \(\mu_{0x}\), its \((D(1),R(1))\) margin is \(\mu_{1x}\), it assigns probability one to \(D(0)\le D(1)\), and each fixed within-arm margin obeys the semicompeting-risk order.  This defines the latent compatibility class independently of \(\Theta_I(P)\).

Necessity is immediate but measure-valued.  If \(\nu_x\) is the \((D(0),R(1))\) projection of \(Q_x\), then it has margins \(d_x\) and \(\zeta_x\).  For every finite \(u\) and Borel \(B\subseteq\mathcal E\), terminal monotonicity gives the set inclusion
\[
 \{D(0)>u,R(1)\in B\}\subseteq\{D(1)>u,R(1)\in B\}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \nu_x((u,\infty]\times B)
 \le \mu_{1x}((u,\infty]\times B)=K_x(u,B),
\]
so \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\).  Notice that this proves the inequality for every mark set \(B\), not only after marginalizing over \(R(1)\).

For sufficiency, fix \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\).  Both \(\nu_x\) and \(\mu_{1x}\) have second margin \(\zeta_x\).  Construct conditional distribution functions \(F_{0x}(q\mid v)\) and \(F_{1x}(q\mid v)\) at rational \(q\in[0,\tau]\) by taking Radon--Nikodym derivatives, with respect to \(\zeta_x\), of
\[
 B\longmapsto\nu_x([0,q]\times B),
 \qquad
 B\longmapsto\mu_{1x}([0,q]\times B).
\]
Choose versions simultaneously monotone in rational \(q\), and extend them by right continuity; the extension includes the isolated point \(\infty\).  This is an explicit disintegration on the ordered compact carrier: equality on the rational threshold generating class implies equality for every Borel subset of \(\mathcal E^2\).

For each rational \(u\), the capacity inequality for all \(B\) implies the corresponding Radon--Nikodym inequality
\[
 1-F_{0x}(u\mid v)\le 1-F_{1x}(u\mid v)
 \quad\text{for \(\zeta_x\)-almost every \(v\)}.
\]
There are only countably many rational \(u\), so one null set works for all of them.  Right continuity then gives
\[
 F_{0x}(u\mid v)\ge F_{1x}(u\mid v)
 \quad\text{for every finite \(u\)}
\]
outside that single null set.  Define the generalized inverse
\[
 Q_{ax}(w,v)=\inf\{q\in\mathbb Q\cap[0,\tau]:F_{ax}(q\mid v)\ge w\},
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
with value \(\infty\) if the set is empty.  Its measurability follows from
\(\{Q_{ax}\le q\}=\{w\le F_{ax}(q\mid v)\}\) at rational \(q\).  If \(V\sim\zeta_x\) and \(W\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) independently, set
\[
 D(0)=Q_{0x}(W,V),\qquad D(1)=Q_{1x}(W,V),\qquad R(1)=V.
\]
The conditional CDF order implies \(Q_{0x}(W,V)\le Q_{1x}(W,V)\) almost surely.  The two required projected margins follow from the inverse-transform identity.  On the exceptional null set choose the same fixed point for both deaths, which preserves all margins.

Finally disintegrate \(\mu_{0x}\) with respect to its death margin \(d_x\), and, conditionally on the constructed \(D(0)\), draw \(R(0)\) from that kernel.  Then
\[
 \mathcal L(D(0),R(0)\mid X=x)=\mu_{0x},\qquad
 \mathcal L(D(1),R(1)\mid X=x)=\mu_{1x}.
\]
The strict within-arm event orders are inherited from these fixed margins, while the cross-arm terminal order was built into the common-quantile draw.  Since \(\mathcal X\) is finite, these cellwise kernels paste measurably.  Draw \(X\) with probabilities \(p_x\), draw \(Z\) with propensity \(e(x)\) independently of all potential outcomes conditional on \(X\), and draw \(C\) from its observed conditional law independently of the potential path.  Consistency then produces the same within-arm event laws, propensity, covariate masses, and censoring law as \(P\).  The IPCW lemma shows that these are precisely the identified complete arm margins.

It remains to connect the latent law to the causal target.  Under \(D(0)\le D(1)\),
\[
 \{D(0)>t,D(1)>t\}=\{D(0)>t\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal H_\eta\), the target-domain definition gives \(S(t)\ge\eta>0\).  Conditioning first on \(X=x\) and then standardizing therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\{R(1)\le r\mid D(0)>t,D(1)>t\}
 -\Pr\{R(0)\le r\mid D(0)>t,D(1)>t\}
 =\frac{\sum_xp_x\{\nu_x((t,\infty]\times[0,r])-b_x(r,t)\}}{S(t)}.
\]
For \(0\le a\le t\), Tonelli's theorem applied to
\(\min\{q,a\}=a-\int_0^a\mathbf 1\{q\le r\}\,dr\) gives
\[
 E[\min\{R(1),a\}-\min\{R(0),a\}\mid D(0)>t]
 =-\int_0^a\theta_\nu(r,t)\,dr=\rho_\nu(a,t).
\]
Thus every compatible full law maps into the displayed surface image, and the measurable lift shows that every point of that image is attained by a compatible full law reproducing \(P\).  This proves equality, hence sharpness, rather than merely an outer bound.

The proof uses conservation on a nested chain and finite linear-program duality.  Fix \(x\), suppress it in the notation, and index ordered death categories by \(i=0,\ldots,m\), with the last category representing \(\infty\).  For a projected table \(f\), its two margins are exactly
\[
 \sum_j f_{ij}=d_x(i),\qquad \sum_i f_{ij}=\zeta_x(j).
\]
On a grid, the defining capacity inequality for the singleton mark \(\{j\}\) is
\[
 \sum_{i>k}f_{ij}\le \mu_{1x}(D(1)>k,R(1)=j)=\kappa^x_{kj}.
\]
Summing these singleton inequalities proves the capacity inequality for every grid mark set, and choosing singleton sets proves the converse.  Hence these inequalities and the two margins are equivalent to \(f\in\mathcal N_x\).

For the network construction, create chain nodes \(v_{0j},\ldots,v_{mj}\) for each \(j\), inject \(\zeta_x(j)\) at \(v_{0j}\), put an exit of size \(f_{ij}\) from \(v_{ij}\) to death-demand node \(i\), and give the arc \(v_{kj}\to v_{k+1,j}\) capacity \(\kappa^x_{kj}\).  Conservation at the first \(k+1\) nodes forces the arc load to be
\[
 q_{kj}=\zeta_x(j)-\sum_{i\le k}f_{ij}=\sum_{i>k}f_{ij}.
\]
Thus a feasible table defines a feasible network flow.  Conversely, reading the exit flows from any feasible network gives the two margins and \(q_{kj}\le\kappa^x_{kj}\), so it gives a feasible table.  There are \(O(m^2)\) chain and exit arcs and \(O(m^2)\) nodes when both axes have \(m\) levels.  The full-law lift follows from the finite specialization of the capacity-projection theorem; no additional response-type coordinates are required.

For completeness, write the support primal in one cell as
\[
 \max_{f\ge0}\ \sum_{i,j}c^x_{ij}f_{ij}
\]
subject to the two margin equalities and the tail inequalities above.  For free multipliers \(\alpha_i,\beta_j\) on the equalities and nonnegative multipliers \(\lambda_{kj}\) on the tail inequalities, any dual-feasible tuple satisfies
\[
 \alpha_i+\beta_j+\sum_{k<i}\lambda_{kj}\ge c^x_{ij}.
\]
Multiplying by \(f_{ij}\), summing, and using \(\lambda_{kj}\ge0\) gives the weak-duality chain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{i,j}c^x_{ij}f_{ij}
 &\le\sum_{i,j}\left(\alpha_i+\beta_j+\sum_{k<i}\lambda_{kj}\right)f_{ij}\\
 &=\sum_i\alpha_i d_x(i)+\sum_j\beta_j\zeta_x(j)
   +\sum_{k,j}\lambda_{kj}\sum_{i>k}f_{ij}\\
 &\le\sum_i\alpha_i d_x(i)+\sum_j\beta_j\zeta_x(j)
   +\sum_{k,j}\lambda_{kj}\kappa^x_{kj}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The primal feasible set is a closed subset of the probability simplex, hence compact, and a signed cost is bounded on it.  The cited finite strong-duality lemma therefore gives equality and attainment for the displayed node-potential dual.  Cells \(x\) have no shared unknown constraints, so summing their optimal values gives \(h_m(c)\) exactly.

The proof uses nested-deadline matching, its suffix cuts, and compact limiting arguments.  Fix \(x\) and \(t\), and put \(s=s_x(t)\).  The case \(s=0\) is immediate because the infinity cut gives \(A_x^U=A_x^L=0\), so assume \(s>0\).  In any compatible lift, the treated records paired to \(D(0)>t\) form a submeasure \(w\le\mu_{1x}\) of total mass \(s\), supported on \(D(1)>t\), and for every \(u\ge t\)
\[
 w(D(1)>u)\ge \Pr(D(0)>u\mid X=x)=s_x(u).
\]
For a Borel mark set \(B\), split selected records at the deadline \(u\).  At most \(s-s_x(u)\) selected records can have \(D(1)\le u\), while at most \(K_x(u,B)\) available \(B\)-records have \(D(1)>u\).  Therefore
\[
 w(R(1)\in B)\le s-s_x(u)+K_x(u,B)
\]
for every \(u\in[t,\tau]\), and the isolated cut \(u=\infty\) gives the bound \(s\).  Hence
\[
 w(R(1)\in B)\le
 \inf_{u\in[t,\tau]\cup\{\infty\}}\{s-s_x(u)+K_x(u,B)\}.
\]

We next prove attainability.  On a finite rational grid, multiply all masses by a common denominator.  Make one demand copy for each unit of the control margin with death after \(t\), and one resource copy for each unit of the treated \((D(1),R(1))\) margin with death after \(t\).  A resource of death level \(h\) is adjacent precisely to demand copies of death level \(i\le h\).  Marginal terminal dominance, obtained by taking \(B=\mathcal E\) in the capacity projection, says that every suffix has at least as many resources as demands, so a matching covering all \(s\) demands exists.

For the subcollection of resources marked by \(B\), the upper bound above is the complete obstruction.  Indeed, run the augmenting-path matching algorithm on the \(B\)-resources.  If it stops before the claimed number, let \(A\) be the demands reachable by alternating paths from unmatched \(B\)-resources.  Nested adjacency implies that \(A\) is a terminal suffix: replacing it by the suffix beginning at its earliest element does not enlarge its resource neighborhood and cannot increase the number of demands outside \(A\).  The absence of an augmenting path then gives
\[
 \#\{\text{matched \(B\)-resources}\}
 =\#\{\text{demands outside \(A\)}\}
  +\#\{\text{\(B\)-resources adjacent to \(A\)}\},
\]
which is exactly one of the displayed deadline cuts.  Thus the maximum is the minimum over suffix cuts.  Any maximizing partial matching extends to a matching of all demands: superpose it with a full matching; alternating paths and cycles add unmatched resources without deleting an already selected one.  This proves the cut formula on rational grids without assuming integrality.

The matchable resource sets satisfy augmentation by the same alternating-path argument.  Order resources by increasing readmission category and greedily accept a resource whenever matchability is preserved.  After every prefix, the accepted resources form a maximal matchable subset of that prefix; augmentation makes its size equal to the prefix rank.  Extending the final independent set to a full matching therefore produces one coupling that attains the upper cut value for every readmission prefix simultaneously.  Reversing the readmission order maximizes every complementary suffix, and hence simultaneously minimizes every prefix.

For arbitrary real finite masses, approximate one feasible full table by rational full tables on the same allowed cells.  Their induced margins and every finite cut value converge.  The rational extremizers lie in a fixed finite simplex; a convergent subsequence has the desired limiting margins, preserves the closed order \(D(0)\le D(1)\), and attains the limiting cuts.  For continuous time, refine finite partitions containing \(t\) and any prescribed finite set of readmission thresholds, while isolating \(\infty\).  The weak-compactness lemma supplies a convergent subsequence of the full couplings.  Fixed finite-part densities imply zero mass on every finite threshold boundary, and
\[
 |K_x(u,B)-K_x(v,B)|\le\Pr\{u<D(1)\le v\mid X=x\}\le M|u-v|
\]
for \(u<v\).  Thus the discrete suffix minima converge to the continuum infimum, and the limit coupling attains every threshold in the chosen finite list.  The closed optimizing sets in the compact fixed-margin fiber consequently have the finite-intersection property.  Their intersection supplies one upper coupling for all \(r\le t\); reverse ordering supplies one lower coupling for all \(r\le t\).

Taking \(B=[0,r]\) gives exactly \(A_x^U(r,t)\).  Applying the upper result to \(B=(r,\infty]\) and subtracting from total selected mass \(s\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \min_\nu\nu_x(D(0)>t,R(1)\le r)
 &=s-\inf_u\{s-s_x(u)+K_x(u,(r,\infty])\}\\
 &=\sup_u\{s_x(u)-K_x(u,(r,\infty])\}=A_x^L(r,t).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For a fixed cohort \(t\), choose the common extremizer separately in each of the finitely many cells.  Since \(p_x/S(t)\ge0\) and \(S(t)>0\) on the target domain, summing the cell endpoints and subtracting the fixed \(b_x(r,t)\) gives the standardized sharp TV-SACE envelopes.  Finally every compatible surface satisfies \(\theta^L(r,t)\le\theta_\nu(r,t)\le\theta^U(r,t)\).  Hence, for \(0\le a\le t\),
\[
 -\int_0^a\theta^U(r,t)\,dr
 \le\rho_\nu(a,t)\le
 -\int_0^a\theta^L(r,t)\,dr.
\]
The common upper and lower couplings just constructed attain the left and right endpoints, respectively.  The RM interval is therefore sharp; pointwise integration is justified here by common fixed-cohort extremizers, not by coordinatewise sharpness alone.

The proof is an exact finite-table certificate followed by a separated smoothing argument.  In the exhibit, \(R(0)=\infty\), so \(b(r,t)=0\).  The control survivor masses at \(t=1,2,3\) are \(3/4,1/2,1/4\), respectively.  The restriction \(0<\eta\le1/4\) places all three displayed indices in \(\mathcal H_\eta\), including its boundary when \(\eta=1/4\).

Use the deadline formulas with the displayed capacity array.  At \((r,t)=(1,1)\), the prefix is column \(0\), and
\[
 A^U(1,1)=\min\{1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 3/4\}=1/5,
 \qquad
 A^L(1,1)=\max\{1/20, -1/20, -1/20, 0\}=1/20.
\]
At \((2,2)\), the prefix is columns \(0,1\), and
\[
 A^U(2,2)=\min\{1/4, 2/5, 1/2\}=1/4,
 \qquad
 A^L(2,2)=\max\{1/20, 0, 0\}=1/20.
\]
At \((3,3)\), the prefix is columns \(0,1,2\), and
\[
 A^U(3,3)=\min\{1/5, 1/4\}=1/5,
 \qquad
 A^L(3,3)=\max\{1/20, 0\}=1/20.
\]
Dividing by the corresponding survivor masses yields
\[
 \theta_\nu(1,1)\in[1/15,4/15],\qquad
 \theta_\nu(2,2)\in[1/10,1/2],\qquad
 \theta_\nu(3,3)\in[1/5,4/5].
\]

Direct summation of the explicitly listed nonzero entries in the definition gives, for each sign,
\[
 \left(\sum_hq^{\pm}_{ihj}\right)_{ij}=f^{\pm},
 \qquad
 \left(\sum_iq^{\pm}_{ihj}\right)_{hj}=\mu_1^\star.
\]
For example, for the minus lift these two aggregations, multiplied by \(100\), are
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}10&0&10&5\\0&10&5&10\\15&5&0&5\\0&5&0&20\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}5&0&0&5\\5&10&0&5\\5&5&10&10\\10&5&5&20\end{pmatrix},
\]
and for the plus lift they are
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}5&0&10&10\\10&15&0&0\\0&0&0&25\\10&5&5&5\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}5&0&0&5\\5&10&0&5\\5&5&10&10\\10&5&5&20\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Every listed nonzero \(q^\pm_{ihj}\) has \(i\le h\).  Thus both lifts satisfy \(D(0)\le D(1)\), have the treated margin \(\mu_1^\star\), and, after attaching \(R(0)=\infty\), have the control margin \(\mu_0^\star\).  Their projected row sums are \((1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), their column sums are \((1/4,1/5,3/20,2/5)\), and the chain loads printed in the definition are entrywise no larger than \(\kappa^\star\).  Nonnegativity and every capacity constraint are therefore certified.

Expanding the three standardized coordinates in \(\ell_\star\) cancels all but four cells:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \ell_\star(\nu)
 &=\sum_{i>0}f_{i0}-\sum_{i>1,\,j\le1}f_{ij}
   +\sum_{i>2,\,j\le2}f_{ij}\\
 &=f_{10}-f_{21}+f_{30}+f_{32}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The upper certificate is
\[
 \ell_\star(\nu)
 \le f_{10}+f_{30}+f_{32}
 \le\sum_{i>0}f_{i0}+\sum_{i>2}f_{i2}
 \le\kappa^\star_{00}+\kappa^\star_{22}=1/4.
\]
For the lower certificate, the capacities and last row give
\[
 f_{21}+f_{31}\le\kappa^\star_{11}=1/10,
 \qquad
 f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32}=1/4-f_{33}\ge1/4-\kappa^\star_{23}=1/20.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \ell_\star(\nu)
 =f_{10}-(f_{21}+f_{31})+(f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32})\ge-1/20.
\]
Substitution gives \(\ell_\star(f^-)=-1/20\) and \(\ell_\star(f^+)=1/4\), so the interval is sharp.  The rectangle formed from the three coordinate intervals has endpoints
\[
 \frac34\frac1{15}-\frac12\frac12+\frac14\frac15=-\frac3{20},
 \qquad
 \frac34\frac4{15}-\frac12\frac1{10}+\frac14\frac45=\frac7{20},
\]
which strictly contain \([-1/20,1/4]\).

For smoothing, choose a symmetric continuously differentiable density supported in \((-\delta,\delta)\), with \(\delta<1/8\), and translate it to every finite death and readmission category.  Use product draws within each positive treated cell.  All finite readmission supports then remain strictly below their associated death supports.  In a lift cell with \(i=h\), use the same translated death draw for \(D(0)\) and \(D(1)\); when \(i<h\), the separated supports themselves imply \(D(0)<D(1)\).  The finite-part marginal densities are bounded and Lipschitz for some finite envelopes \(M\) and \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\), and all threshold classifications at \(1,2,3\) are unchanged, so all displayed support values remain unchanged.  The remaining maintained conditions hold because \(X\) is degenerate with positive mass, \(e=1/2\) satisfies every declared overlap floor, and \(C=\tau=3\) gives \(G_{zx}(u)=1\ge\gamma\) throughout the horizon.  Finally, with the categorical support cells fixed, every endpoint is the value of a finite linear program with fixed constraint matrix and continuously varying right-hand side.  Such a value is piecewise linear on its feasible parameter cone.  The strict gaps \(1/10\) and \(1/5\) from the two rectangular endpoints therefore persist throughout a sufficiently small relatively open neighborhood of the smoothed law in the maintained model.

The proof uses weak compactness, a uniform modulus, and two-sided approximation of feasible fibers.  Fix the identified margins.  Let \(\mathcal Q_x\) be the laws on \(\mathcal E^4\) having the two fixed within-arm margins and satisfying \(D(0)\le D(1)\).  The ambient law space is weakly compact by the cited compact-carrier lemma.  Marginalization is weakly continuous, and \(\{D(0)\le D(1)\}\) is closed because \(\infty\) is isolated and maximal.  Hence \(\mathcal Q_x\) is closed and compact.  The strict within-arm order creates no nonclosed constraint here: every member and every limit has the same fixed within-arm margins, which assign probability one to the semicompeting-risk support.  The capacity-projection theorem identifies the projection of \(\mathcal Q_x\) with \(\mathcal N_x\), so each \(\mathcal N_x\), and their finite product over \(x\), is compact and convex.

We next establish continuity in the claimed uniform norm.  For \(r,r',t,t'\in[0,\tau]\), any \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\) satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|\nu_x((t,\infty]\times[0,r])-\nu_x((t',\infty]\times[0,r'])\right|\\
 &\qquad\le d_x((t\wedge t',t\vee t'])+\zeta_x((r\wedge r',r\vee r'])
 \le M(|t-t'|+|r-r'|).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The same bound applies to changes of \(b_x(r,t)\), up to another factor of two, and
\(|S(t)-S(t')|\le M|t-t'|\).  On \(\mathcal H_\eta\), \(S\ge\eta>0\).  The quotient identity
\[
 \left|\frac{N}{S}-\frac{N'}{S'}\right|
 \le \frac{|N-N'|}{\eta}+\frac{|N'|\,|S-S'|}{\eta^2}
\]
therefore gives a common Lipschitz modulus for all \(\theta_\nu\).  Since \(S\) is continuous, \(\mathcal H_\eta\) is a closed subset of the compact triangle \(\{(r,t):0\le r\le t\le\tau\}\), hence is compact.  Integration gives a common modulus for \(\rho_\nu\) as well.

If \(\nu^{(q)}_x\Rightarrow\nu_x\), every finite threshold rectangle used above is a continuity set because the fixed death and readmission margins have finite-part densities.  Thus \(\theta_{\nu^{(q)}}\to\theta_\nu\) pointwise.  The common modulus and a finite-net argument upgrade this to uniform convergence on the compact target domain \(\mathcal H_\eta\); the integral definition then gives uniform convergence of \(\rho\).  Hence the surface map is continuous from a compact convex fiber into \(C(\mathcal H_\eta)^2\).  Its image \(\Theta_I(P)\) is compact.  It is convex because the unknown numerator and the RM integral are affine in \(\nu\), while \(S\) and \(b_x\) are fixed.  Every continuous signed support functional consequently attains its maximum and minimum on \(\Theta_I(P)\).

It remains to prove grid convergence.  Let nested partitions have finite mesh \(\delta_m\downarrow0\), isolate \(\infty\), retain the observed within-bin event-order mark, and use one fixed multilinear interpolation on the triangular index domain.  Denote the resulting exact chain-flow surface set by \(K_m\) and the continuous set by \(K=\Theta_I(P)\).  For any \(Q\in\prod_x\mathcal Q_x\), push every finite coordinate to its grid cell and retain its order mark.  The projected table obeys every suffix capacity because the set inclusion \(D(0)>u\Rightarrow D(1)>u\) survives coarsening.  At all grid thresholds its numerator differs from the continuous numerator only on boundary strips of width at most \(\delta_m\), whose probability is at most \(M\delta_m\) per coordinate.  The common quotient modulus then gives
\[
 \sup_{q\in K}\inf_{q_m\in K_m}\|q-q_m\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
\]

Conversely, take any sequence \(q_m\in K_m\) and choose its finite-grid full-law lift supplied by the chain-flow theorem.  Embed each grid coordinate at a point in its cell.  The embedded within-arm margins converge to the fixed margins.  Grid monotonicity implies \(D_m(0)\le D_m(1)+\delta_m\); hence every weak subsequential limit satisfies the closed order \(D(0)\le D(1)\).  Compactness gives such a subsequence, and its limit lies in \(\prod_x\mathcal Q_x\).  A finite grid atom has mass at most the fixed marginal mass of one cell, hence at most \(M\delta_m\) on the finite part.  The interpolated grid surfaces therefore obey the preceding common modulus with an additional term tending to zero.  Pointwise convergence at continuity thresholds and the finite-net argument show that the chosen subsequence converges uniformly to the surface of its limiting compatible law.  If
\[
 \sup_{q_m\in K_m}\inf_{q\in K}\|q_m-q\|_\infty
\]
did not tend to zero, a maximizing countersequence and this subsequence argument would contradict the positive lower bound.  Combining the two directed limits proves \(d_H(K_m,K)\to0\).

For any continuous linear functional \(L\),
\[
 \left|\sup_{q_m\in K_m}L(q_m)-\sup_{q\in K}L(q)\right|
 \le \|L\|\,d_H(K_m,K)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Finally, fixed-cohort RM endpoints are integrals of the common sharp TV envelopes.  Their integrands have the same uniform modulus and converge uniformly, so
\[
 \left|\int_0^a\theta_m^{U,L}(r,t)\,dr-
       \int_0^a\theta^{U,L}(r,t)\,dr\right|
 \le a\,\|\theta_m^{U,L}-\theta^{U,L}\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves convergence of both sharp RM endpoints without assuming that independently selected grid optimizers are projectively consistent.

The proof combines a conditional exponential-moment bound with deterministic propagation through the moment region.  First consider a Bernoulli mean based on \(N>0\) observations.  For \(B\in\{0,1\}\) with mean \(q\), put \(\psi(\lambda)=\log E\exp\{\lambda(B-q)\}\).  Exponential tilting keeps a Bernoulli law, so \(\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0\) and \(\psi''(\lambda)=q_\lambda(1-q_\lambda)\le1/4\), where \(q_\lambda\in[0,1]\) is its tilted success probability.  Taylor's formula with integral remainder, applied also at negative \(\lambda\), gives
\[
 E\exp\{\lambda(B-q)\}\le\exp(\lambda^2/8).
\]
Independence and Markov's inequality consequently give
\[
 \Pr(\bar B_N-q\ge r)
 \le\inf_{\lambda>0}\exp\{-\lambda Nr+N\lambda^2/8\}
 =e^{-2Nr^2},
\]
where the infimum is attained at \(\lambda=4r\).  Applying the same calculation to \(-B\) and adding the two tails yields
\[
 \Pr(|\bar B_N-q|>r)\le2e^{-2Nr^2}.
\]
Conditional on the complete vector of treatment--covariate cell counts, observations within each nonempty cell are independent draws from that conditional cell law.  With
\[
 r_{zx}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2J/\alpha)}{2N_{zx}}},
\]
each two-sided primitive interval fails with conditional probability at most \(\alpha/J\).  The identical calculation with \(N=n\) applies to each \(\widehat p_x\).  Zero-count cells have interval \([0,1]\) and cannot fail.  Since \(J\) counts all primitive and covariate-mass intervals, a union bound, followed by averaging over the random counts, yields
\[
 \inf_P\Pr_P(\mathscr E_n)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
No uniform lower bound on the realized counts is used; treatment overlap only guarantees that every population treatment--covariate cell associated with a supported \(x\) is well defined.

We now verify the deterministic observation restrictions on \(\mathscr E_n\).  Fix \((z,x)\).  Independent censoring gives
\[
 A^{zx}_{ij}=\int_{I_i\times B_j}G_{zx}(d)\,\mu_{zx}(d d,d r).
\]
Because \(G_{zx}\) is nonincreasing and \(a_i\le d<a_{i+1}\),
\[
 g^{zx}_{i+1}\pi^{zx}_{ij}\le A^{zx}_{ij}\le g^{zx}_i\pi^{zx}_{ij}.
\]
At an exact discrete death time there is no within-bin variation, and this becomes equality.  Similarly, independence at the deterministic times \(a_i\) and \(\tau\) gives
\[
 Y^{zx}_i=g^{zx}_i\left\{\sum_{h\ge i,j}\pi^{zx}_{hj}+\sum_j\pi^{zx}_{\infty j}\right\},
 \qquad
 V^{zx}_j=g^{zx}_m\pi^{zx}_{\infty j}.
\]
The survival-function definition and full-horizon support give
\[
 1\ge g^{zx}_0\ge\cdots\ge g^{zx}_m\ge\gamma>0.
\]
The true arm tables are probability simplices and inherit the semicompeting event-order restriction.  On \(\mathscr E_n\), every true observable moment and every \(p_x\) also lies in its stipulated interval.  Thus the true coarsened primitive vector, together with its true censoring vector, is an element of \(\mathcal B_n\).

Take any surface in \(\Theta_I(P)\) and restrict it to \(\mathcal G_m\).  Coarsen its projected coupling \(\nu_x\) into the same death and mark bins.  Its margins are the true coarsened \(d_x,\zeta_x\), and, for every cut \(k\) and mark bin \(j\),
\[
 \sum_{i>k}f^x_{ij}
 =\nu_x(D(0)>a_k,R(1)\in B_j)
 \le K_x(a_k,B_j)=\kappa^x_{kj}.
\]
The chain-flow theorem makes this an exact grid surface in the image attached to the true primitive vector.  Since that vector lies in \(\mathcal B_n\) on \(\mathscr E_n\), the definition of the union \(\mathcal C_n\) gives the deterministic inclusion
\[
 \Theta_I(P)|_{\mathcal G_m}\subseteq\mathcal C_n
 \qquad\text{on \(\mathscr E_n\)}.
\]
Taking probabilities and the preceding uniform concentration bound proves
\[
 \inf_P\Pr_P\{\Theta_I(P)|_{\mathcal G_m}\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}
 \ge1-\alpha.
\]
The argument uses one simultaneous primitive event and never differentiates an optimal flow face.  It is therefore unchanged when active cuts tie or change.

Assume the displayed no-terminal-effect premise as a restriction on the compatible full laws.  Then the two identified death margins coincide.  For any \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\), define finite measures on the readmission space by
\[
 q_{x,t}(B)=\nu_x((t,\infty]\times B),
 \qquad
 k_{x,t}(B)=\mu_{1x}(D(1)>t,R(1)\in B).
\]
The capacity restriction says \(q_{x,t}(B)\le k_{x,t}(B)\) for every Borel \(B\).  Equality of the death margins gives
\[
 q_{x,t}(\mathcal E)=d_x((t,\infty])
 =\Pr(D(1)>t\mid X=x)=k_{x,t}(\mathcal E).
\]
Applying the capacity inequality to \(B^c\) yields
\[
 q_{x,t}(B)=q_{x,t}(\mathcal E)-q_{x,t}(B^c)
 \ge k_{x,t}(\mathcal E)-k_{x,t}(B^c)=k_{x,t}(B).
\]
Thus \(q_{x,t}=k_{x,t}\), and in particular
\[
 \nu_x(D(0)>t,R(1)\le r)
 =\mu_{1x}(D(1)>t,R(1)\le r).
\]
The control term \(b_x(r,t)\), the denominator \(S(t)\), and both within-arm measures are identified from \(P\) by the IPCW lemma.  Substitution into the TV surface formula leaves no dependence on \(\nu\); integration leaves no dependence in the RM surface either.  The capacity-projection theorem says every compatible surface is represented by some \(\nu\in\prod_x\mathcal N_x\), so \(\Theta_I(P)\) is the singleton ordinary standardized within-arm cumulative-incidence contrast among the common survivor cohort.  This proves point identification from the premise; it does not define point identification into existence.

Conversely, every measurable family \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\) admits a measurable full-law lift of \((D(0),R(0),D(1),R(1))\) that preserves both \(\mu_{0x}\) and \(\mu_{1x}\), satisfies \(D(0)\le D(1)\), and reproduces \(P\).

proposed.gap: Comment et al. define the surface but parameterize its cross-world law; Chen, Cui, and Yang bound a fixed scalar survivor outcome; generic transport results do not prove the marked conditional projection or full-law lift.
proposed.consumer: It gives clinicians every conclusion about the complete TV-SACE/RM-SACE surface that follows from treatment exchangeability, full follow-up support, and audited terminal monotonicity alone.

The network has \(O(m^2)\) nodes and arcs when both time axes have \(m\) levels, every feasible flow lifts to a full law, and \(h_m(c)\) equals the stated node-potential dual for every signed cost \(c\).

proposed.gap: Russell and Ober-Reynolds provide generic latent-law programs and duals; neither source gives this nested chain, its complete suffix cuts, or the reconstruction of full semicompeting-risk laws.
proposed.consumer: It supplies an exact auditable algorithm for the finite-horizon grids used in the Comment et al. analysis and a certificate for every reported support endpoint.

proposed.statement: For each fixed \(t\) and cell \(x\), the sharp extrema of \(\nu_x(D(0)>t,R(1)\le r)\) are \(A^L_x(r,t)\) and \(A^U_x(r,t)\). One coupling attains \(A^U_x(r,t)\) simultaneously for every \(r\le t\), and another coupling attains \(A^L_x(r,t)\) simultaneously for every \(r\le t\). Therefore the standardized coordinate bounds follow by summing with weights \(p_x/S(t)\), and the sharp RM-SACE interval is obtained by integrating the opposite common TV-SACE envelopes along that fixed cohort.
proposed.justification: Coordinatewise sharpness does not justify integration; common extremizers are the missing mathematical reason that fixed-cohort RM-SACE envelope integration is exact.
proposed.gap: Chen, Cui, and Yang integrate threshold bounds for a scalar survivor outcome, while the opened papers do not prove one coupling jointly attains all readmission thresholds for a nested survivor cohort.
proposed.consumer: It gives a closed-form RM-SACE sensitivity region without solving a new optimization problem at every integration point.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A joint uniform asymptotic-linear expansion for a fully specified marked complete-path estimator with estimated administrative-censoring survival, plus conditional consistency of its increment-level multiplier process after applying all upper and lower endpoint maps.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handle does not define the censoring-survival estimator, its filtration and influence function, the marked arm-law estimator, or the multiplier weights. The supplied assumptions alone therefore do not determine the stochastic process whose functional central limit theorem and conditional law must be proved. Unique cuts settle the population envelope derivative but do not supply this missing primitive statistical theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the active-cut envelope derivative, the quotient derivative including estimated covariate weights, the complementary-cut lower derivative, RM integration, and an order bound for deterministic grid bias. A generic empirical-process composition cannot complete the proof without first specifying and proving the joint marked product-limit or IPCW influence representation with estimated censoring through the horizon.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The population endpoint map has the following proved derivative at a unique upper deadline cut.  Write \(F_\epsilon=F+\epsilon H_\epsilon\), where \(H_\epsilon\to H\) uniformly, and let \(u_\epsilon\) minimize \(F_\epsilon\).  Compactness of the cut domain and uniqueness of \(u_x^\star\) imply \(u_\epsilon\to u_x^\star\): otherwise a convergent subsequence would have a distinct limit minimizing \(F\).  The two optimality inequalities
\[
 F_\epsilon(u_\epsilon)\le F_\epsilon(u_x^\star),
 \qquad F(u_x^\star)\le F(u_\epsilon)
\]
sandwich the difference quotient between \(H_\epsilon(u_\epsilon)+o(1)\) and \(H_\epsilon(u_x^\star)+o(1)\).  Both converge to \(H(u_x^\star)\).  Thus, for a primitive perturbation \(h=(h_{p_x},h_{s_x},h_{K_x},h_{b_x})\),
\[
 dA_x^U(r,t)[h]=h_{s_x}(t)-h_{s_x}(u_x^\star)+h_{K_x}(u_x^\star,[0,r]),
\]
with both perturbation terms at \(\infty\) set to zero.  If \(N=\sum_xp_x(A_x-b_x)\) and \(S=\sum_xp_xs_x\), then
\[
 d\theta[h]=\frac{dN[h]-\theta\,dS[h]}{S},
\]
where
\[
 dN[h]=\sum_x\{h_{p_x}(A_x-b_x)+p_x(dA_x[h]-h_{b_x})\},
 \qquad
 dS[h]=\sum_x\{h_{p_x}s_x+p_xh_{s_x}\}.
\]
The lower derivative follows by applying the same formula to the complementary mark set, and \(d\rho(a,t)[h]=-\int_0^a d\theta(r,t)[h]\,dr\).  Bounded finite-part densities give deterministic interpolation bias \(O(\delta_m)\), so \(\delta_m=o(n^{-1/2})\) makes that bias negligible.  What remains unproved is the joint uniform asymptotic-linear representation and conditionally valid multiplier approximation for a precisely defined estimated-censoring marked-path estimator.
